thread:
lina: hey team :wave: first day — I'm blocked on secrets. trying to read the service creds at `secret/data/svc/redwood/frontend` and get permission denied. who should I ask for access?
sam: welcome! can you paste the exact path and the error message? also which repo/service is this for?
lina: path is `secret/data/svc/redwood/frontend/api-key`. error: "permission denied" from vault CLI when running `vault kv get secret/data/svc/redwood/frontend/api-key`.
sam: okay. quick checklist: 1) are you on the company VPN/VPC? 2) did you authenticate to Vault (oidc) with `vault login -method=oidc`? 3) do you have the team label on your account? if you don't know, say which team and I'll check.
lina: I'm on corp VPN. I did `vault login` via the browser SSO earlier. team is frontend-platform.
sam: thanks. frontend-platform secrets are gated by the `team/frontend-platform` policy. @june_security do we require a specific approval flow for new-hires on that policy?
june_security: hi — for user-level read access we need: a ticket in the onboarding form + an approval from the team's owner group. We try to grant vault read rights within 1 business day for new-hires once approvals are in place. KMS key access is a separate cloud-iam request and can take up to 48 hrs depending on approvals.
lin a: ty. what's the onboarding form link? and what exactly to include in the ticket?
mike_devex: the onboarding form is https://intranet.redwood.com/onboard/secrets (use that form, choose "Vault access"). include: your full email, your team, the secret paths you need, and the reason (e.g., local dev / CI / runtime). attach the repo or infra ticket if applicable.
lina: got it. for CI we actually need the service account key — is there a recommended pattern? do we store service account json in vault or use KMS-wrapped secrets?
june_security: preferred pattern: do NOT store long-lived user keys. For Google cloud: create a workload identity or service account with least privilege and let CI assume it. If you must store credentials, store them in Vault at `secret/data/sa/` with an owner and TTL, and mark them for rotation. We have automation that rotates saved SA keys monthly; manual rotation policy = 90 days for user creds, 30 days for service keys unless automation is configured.
sam: also note: if you need ephemeral credentials for testing, ask SRE to mint short-lived tokens via the secrets-mint service (add `secrets-mint` to your ticket). that avoids long-lived json files.
lin a: sounds good. i submitted the onboarding form just now and put the 3 paths and the repo link.
devex-bot: Your request 2026-ONB-842 has been received. Expected SLA: Vault read access in ~1 business day; KMS grants in up to 48 hours. Please respond in the ticket thread with approvers if asked.
sam: thanks — I see the request. I'll ping the frontend-platform owners for approval now. once approved I'll update you here.
lina: appreciated! small followup — any quick commands to verify once access is granted?
sam: yes: `vault auth list` to verify login method, then `vault kv get secret/data/svc/redwood/frontend/api-key`. if you get a JSON blob, you're good. for GCP KMS: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy ...` won't work for read access but try `gcloud kms keys describe KEY --location=...` to confirm visibility.
june_security: also check that you don't see any policies like `deny-*` in your token. `vault token lookup` will show attached policies.
lina: perfect, thanks everyone :pray:
sam: welcome aboard :tada: ping here if anything stalls.
june_security: welcome — if you need security walkthrough (rotation, audit logs), drop me a calendar invite and i'll run through it.
mike_devex: FYI — internal doc on secret path naming and onboarding lives at https://docs.redwood.com/security/secrets-guidelines
lina: will do, thanks all!"
